memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If a carcass falls on any seeds that are to be planted, they remain clean. But if water has been put on the seed and a carcass falls on it, it is unclean for you." - Lev 11:37-38 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A precise little distinction, and an interesting one. Dry seed stays clean. Wet seed does not.

The difference is absorption. Dry seed simply has a carcass roll off it; nothing penetrates. Once water has been added, the seed has softened and opened, and now what touches it goes in.

There is a picture here of the human heart, though we should hold it lightly. What is hard and closed is not affected — but neither is it growing. Seed only becomes a harvest once it has been softened and opened up. The very openness that makes growth possible is also what makes us vulnerable.

That is simply the reality of following Christ. A soft heart can be hurt. An open life can be wounded. The person who loves deeply can be disappointed deeply. Many of us respond by hardening — deciding never to be that open again.

But Jesus told a parable about seed and soil, and the hard path was not the safe option. It was the barren one (Matt 13:4-8). God's answer to a wounded heart is never a hardened heart. It is a guarded one — guarded not by walls, but by Him. Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it (Prov 4:23).

Stay soft. Stay watchful. Stay near to Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has past hurt made you harder rather than wiser?
2. What does it look like to be open and discerning at the same time?
3. Where do you need God to soften ground that has gone hard?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep my heart soft toward You and toward others, even when softness has cost me. Guard what You have opened, and let good seed grow in me. Amen.
